subject: Throughput uplift runbook and forecasting for PlutoHealth launch
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@plutohealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Quick ask: burst/quota headroom for Jan 31 launch

Hi Kimberly,

Appreciate the quick sync earlier. As we ramp to our public launch on Jan 31st, engineering is pushing a modest uplift to our token throughput for the first 72 hours to handle onboarding traffic and initial sign-up flows.

High-level ask: can Redwood provision a temporary throughput uplift (burst allowance + shorter warmup) to cover ~3M tokens/day for 72 hours (Jan 31 - Feb 2) and a sustained pilot baseline of 600k tokens/day afterwards for the pilot week?

We expect most traffic 02:00-10:00 UTC due to our east-coast user base. Procurement also wants to understand any SLA carveouts or rate-limit exception language we should expect.

I attached our preliminary forecast. Can you loop in product/ops for feasibility and any roadmap caveats?

Thanks,
Alex
Senior Product Manager, PlutoHealth
Attachment: pluto_launch_forecast_v1.xlsx (xlsx)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@plutohealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick ask: burst/quota headroom for Jan 31 launch

Alex — thanks for the forecast and the heads up. Looping in Kar (product) and Marissa (capacity/planning). A couple quick clarifying questions so we can scope the uplift and approvals:

- Is the 3M tokens/day expected as sustained steady traffic during the 72h window or concentrated spikes (e.g., short bursts up to X tokens/min)?
- Can you share the expected sequence length distribution (median, 90th) and percent of requests using streaming vs non-streaming?
- Any PII/PHI escalation or special retention/segmentation requirements?

We can generally support temporary uplifts but need to confirm kernel/profile compatibility for your model variant and whether we'll need a temporary routing policy (regional or tiered fallback). Kar — can you advise on product-level constraints for a 72h uplift and what we need to sign off? Marissa — please advise runway for capacity and whether a soft quota or hard carveout is better here.

Will queue a short 30-min preflight if helpful.

—Kimberly
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachment: sla-exception-request.pdf (pdf)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, Alex Chen <alex.chen@plutohealth.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick ask: burst/quota headroom for Jan 31 launch

Thanks for the loop. Quick product perspective:

- Feasibility: A 72h temporary uplift is supported via a "temp-entitlement" with automatic rollback. We can provision a regional burst allowance tied to the customer API key. Important caveats: model quantization variant must be compatible with our routing fallback; if PlutoHealth is using a custom quantized runtime we need the binary/stdlib details.

- Metrics we need from the customer to size correctly: 90th percentile tokens per request, average requests per minute during peak, and percent streaming. If peak is bursty (e.g., sudden spikes > 200 reqs/min sustained over 5m), we may recommend a short warmup with a staged traffic step to avoid throttle cascades.

- Roadmap caveat: we are rolling out a new batching kernel the week before; we could enable it for this uplift to improve token throughput, but that requires a canary and a signed rollback SLA. If they want that optimization, we need a product sign-off and an ops runbook by Jan 25.

Ask: Kimberly/Marissa, can we offer PlutoHealth the default temp-entitlement (3M/day burst) with a 30% throttle threshold and an optional canary to enable the new batching kernel? If they accept canary, we must capture signoff for rollback and a contact for 24/7 paging during Jan 31-Feb 2.

-Kar
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@plutohealth.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Jan 2028 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick ask: burst/quota headroom for Jan 31 launch

Adding capacity numbers & recommended runbook:

- Capacity: We can allocate the requested 3M tokens/day for the 72h window from our east-us pool, but that will consume ~12% of projected spare capacity for that week. Post-run we can drop them to a sustained 600k/day baseline.

- Traffic profile (based on their sheet): median seq len ~120 tokens, 95th ~420. Streaming calls ~18% of traffic. Peak pattern: several 20–60 second bursts aligned with marketing email sends.

- Recommended runbook: 1) Preflight on Jan 27 for a staged ramp test (10%, 40%, 100%); 2) Enable temp-entitlement Jan 31 00:00 UTC with regional routing to east-us; 3) Activate KV prefix caching for known onboarding prompts; 4) If enabling batching kernel canary, narrow to 10% of their keys for 6 hours pre-launch; 5) On-call contact list + rollback playbook attached.

- Procurement note: standard SLA exceptions acceptable for the uplift (temporary throughput carveout). Any contractual SLA language must reference the temp-entitlement UID we generate.

I'll prepare a short runbook doc and push to the linked Drive folder. We should also capture an acceptance email from procurement for the canary option.

-Marissa
Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
Attachment: pluto_runbook_draft.docx (docx)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@plutohealth.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 17 Jan 2028 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick ask: burst/quota headroom for Jan 31 launch

Alex — thanks, team — thanks for the input. Summary & next steps: 

1) Action for PlutoHealth: confirm whether they want the batching-kernel canary (yes/no) and provide the quantization/runtime details by Jan 19 EOD. Procurement should confirm acceptance of temporary SLA exception referencing UID PLUTO-ENT-20280131 by Jan 20.
2) Internal action (Marissa): create temp-entitlement and runbook in Drive; schedule Jan 27 preflight 14:00 UTC (30-min).
3) Internal action (Kar): prepare canary rollback checklist and acceptance criteria if Pluto opts in.
4) Sales (Kim): send formal quote amendment for the temporary uplift and baseline change to procurement; include link to HubSpot deal and Drive runbook.

If we get their canary signoff, ops will be paged and Kar will own rollback on-call. If they decline, we proceed with the default temp-entitlement with staged ramp.

I'll send a brief summary to procurement and legal to get the exception documented. Meeting invite for the preflight will follow.

—Kim
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Onward: Procurement cc'ed? procurement@plutohealth.com
